absent: Numeric values and bit positions of intercept selectors, control masks and entry masks.
Dirty tracking mechanics for control blocks and source of the global management intercept policy.
Remainder of unaccelerated access handling beyond the trap path and helpers named but not shown in the truncated tail.
Registration of the global address log notifier with input output hardware and matching of wake events.
Global enable flags, extended mode limits and propagation of acceleration inhibit reasons.
Backing page lifetime, access page allocation and encrypted address translation.
Doorbell register encoding and processor cookie derivation.
Busy flag handling and destination matching in the slow interprocessor path.

findings.text: A host routine refreshes nested virtual controls for the active second level guest using cached first level requests and host policy. It is used when nested state changes and expects the current control block to correspond to the second level.

Per machine accelerated interrupt preparation and teardown are available to upper layers. Preparation provisions identifier tables and registers the machine for posted wakeups, while teardown unlinks the machine and releases the tables.

Upper layers can request doorbell signalling for a virtual CPU and can complete interrupt delivery through a helper that selects posted handling or event queueing from acceleration state and execution mode.

Two interception handlers are exposed for hardware reports that acceleration could not complete alone, one for interprocessor interrupts and one for register accesses needing emulation. Both report that the exit was handled.
A query reports whether nested guest mode currently forces inhibition of accelerated handling for a given virtual CPU.

Second level interception policy reflects host first level policy combined with first level guest requests subject to host overrides for management, yielding, save restore virtualization and windowing. Virtual masking suppresses selected interceptions when host injected interrupts cannot be affected.

Virtual save restore instructions need interception unless the guest offers virtualized support together with nested paging and an explicit enable control. Absence of any of those conditions forces interception.

Encrypted guest with extended state is recognized through nested ownership from virtual CPU to virtual machine to vendor info, requiring both enablement flags. An alternate build always reports absence of that guest type.

Machine identifiers for posted interrupts are one based and never zero, allocated monotonically with wrap detection and collision scan, created once and retained until machine destruction. Table allocation is idempotent across multiple virtual CPU creations.

Each virtual CPU publishes a valid physical entry pointing at its backing page so broadcasts observe it, and logical destinations map to at most one entry with explicit validity tracking. Unsupported identifiers inhibit acceleration rather than installing entries.

Accelerated interprocessor handling assumes virtual CPU index equals local identifier and distinguishes physical versus logical destination encodings, with extended mode deriving identity differently and ignoring the logical table. Broadcasts and shorthand forms use a slower scan.

Logical topology tracking follows destination format and leader updates, invalidating the prior mapping as part of installing the new one and ignoring extended mode updates. Only single bit masks with in range clusters are accepted.

A global hash table mapping posted identifiers to machines is guarded by a spin lock taken with interrupts saved during lookup, insertion and removal. Lookups retain the target reference across unlock before waking.
Assignment of a new posted identifier requires holding the virtual machine lock, asserted by the implementation, while the global hash lock serializes concurrent assignments.
Delivery completion orders observation of execution mode before acceleration active flag using acquire semantics paired with release on entry, giving a consistent choice between doorbell and wakeup.

Interception controls are held as a fixed length array of words addressed by numeric selectors through bit operations with range checking. Separate helpers operate on host control areas and on cached nested control areas.

Nested state keeps a cached copy of upper guest controls plus pointers to first level, second level and currently active blocks. A vendor structure for the machine holds encryption info and posted interrupt tables and identifiers.

Per machine acceleration state comprises a numeric identifier, hash linkage, plus physical and logical destination tables whose addresses are programmed into control blocks together with backing page address and default base.

Per virtual CPU acceleration state comprises a cached physical entry value, cached format and leader values, and a backing page derived from the emulated register page. Initialization validates identifier bounds and register presence before publishing.

Nested control refresh is defined only when the active block corresponds to the second level and otherwise leaves state unchanged. When defined its result combines host and guest policies with specific suppressions and assists.
Posted machine lifecycle moves from unregistered to registered on first virtual CPU preparation, remains registered across further preparations, unlinks on pre destroy and frees memory on destroy.

Per virtual CPU backing initialization has distinct outcomes for oversized identifiers, missing register state, need for an access page when acceleration is globally active, and successful publication of a valid entry.

Interrupt completion selects among queueing an event and kicking when acceleration is inactive, ringing a doorbell when the target runs in guest, and waking when blocked. Kicking for acceleration marks pending state and delegates to completion.

Incomplete posted reports dispatch by hardware failure code among emulating unsupported deliveries, kicking sleeping targets whose bits were already set, warning on bad backing configuration, ignoring illegal vectors, and noting unimplemented cases.

Unaccelerated access handling separates trap offsets needing leader, format or read only pre handling from other offsets, with all cases ultimately delegated to generic emulation. Leader and format changes invalidate prior mappings as part of reinstall.

A global address log notifier decodes machine and virtual CPU selectors from a tag, resolves the target under lock, and wakes it to consume a pending bit already set by input output hardware. It always reports success.

Preparation, unlink, free and control initialization form the setup teardown boundary. Preparation is safe to repeat, unlink expects prior registration, and initialization selects activation from current acceleration state.

Doorbell signalling and delivery completion are callable when an interrupt targets a virtual CPU. Doorbell avoids self signalling and tolerates migration, while completion adapts to acceleration and execution mode.
Interception entries for incomplete posted interrupts and unaccelerated accesses decode hardware exit information words into emulation or wakeup actions and return a handled indication.
Refreshing nested interceptions while the active control block is not the second level block is unexpected and leaves state unchanged.
Identifier counter wrap can collide with live machines, so reuse scans for existing use and skips occupied values including skipping zero.

Doorbell target processor is read without locking and the virtual CPU may migrate before signalling, possibly notifying the prior processor. This is treated as harmless because migration is followed by entry processing of pending interrupts.
Oversized virtual CPU identifiers, missing register pages and invalid backing configurations must not install acceleration state. They inhibit, fail initialization or warn respectively.
Bit numbers outside the array capacity are diagnosed rather than silently accepted, in both setting and testing paths.

Deactivation clears acceleration and mode controls and physical index bits and restores selected interceptions and extended register interception, but omits one restore for encrypted guests with extended state.
Logical destination decoding rejects out of range clusters, empty masks and masks that are not a single bit, returning no entry without side effects.

The control interface defines distinct intercept selectors for privileged operations including priority writes, virtual interrupt windowing, management interrupts, pause yielding and virtual save restore.

Nested paging enablement, virtualized save restore enablement, guest capability for virtualized save restore, interrupt masking control and flag interrupt bit govern conditional interception decisions.
Accelerated interrupt control uses enable and mode masks, physical index limits, entry valid and address masks for physical and logical tables, and a default virtual base address.

Interprocessor encodings include destination mode, shorthand, trigger, delivery mode and vector fields plus broadcast values and busy indication, while exit reports pack request words and target index in paired information words.
Posted tags encode machine and virtual CPU selectors with defined extraction and a mask limiting machine identifiers.

Doorbell signalling uses a vendor message register with per processor cookie, and physical identifier bounds differ between base and extended modes with table sizing derived from the maximum supported identifier.

Emulated local register offsets for identity, completion, remote read, leader, format, spurious, error, command, timers and local vectors determine which unaccelerated accesses trap, with flat versus clustered format values affecting decoding.
